question: True or false: bleaching caused most of the coral lost on the Great Barrier Reef between 1985 and 2012?
answer: False. Analysing 27 years of surveys, De'ath and colleagues found coral cover fell from 28% to 14% and put 48% of the loss down to cyclones, 42% to coral-eating crown-of-thorns starfish and 10% to bleaching. The balance has shifted since: from 2016 onwards, repeated marine heatwaves have bleached the reef again and again.
move: Split a loss by cause before choosing which cause to fight.
trap: True, since bleaching is the cause that fills reef news.
reference: De'ath, Fabricius, Sweatman & Puotinen, The 27-year decline of coral cover on the Great Barrier Reef and its causes, PNAS, 2012
